chapters.title: Chapter 8: Careers and the Business of Market Making in India

lessons.title: Who Actually Runs Market Making Books in India: Prop Firms, Bank Desks, and LES Market Makers

body.text: Market making in India is not one job at one type of firm. It is several distinct businesses, split across different instruments, different regulators, and different reasons for existing, and knowing which is which matters before aiming a career at any of them.

children.text: Proprietary Trading Firms: The Dominant Player in Equity and Index Derivatives

Most of the two-sided quoting that keeps Nifty and Bank Nifty options and futures liquid is done by proprietary trading firms, businesses that trade their own capital rather than client money, competing directly on the pricing, inventory, and latency skills covered throughout this course. Some are India-based quant and algorithmic trading firms; others are global high-frequency trading firms with a colocated presence at NSE alongside their operations in other markets. Several such firms, including names that come up regularly in Indian quant finance hiring circles such as Graviton Research Capital, Quadeye, and iRage, are publicly associated with algorithmic and market making activity in Indian derivatives.

body.text: The specific firms named above are mentioned only to illustrate that this category of employer genuinely exists in India, not as a confirmed or exhaustive profile of any firm's current business model, strategies, or hiring needs. Firms enter and exit this space, and their specific activities change; verify anything specific about a particular firm directly before treating it as fact.

children.text: Bank Desks: More Prominent in Currency and Government Bonds Than in Equity Derivatives

markDefs.definition: An entity, typically a bank or a standalone financial institution, granted Primary Dealer status by the RBI, carrying an explicit obligation to underwrite and make continuous two-way markets in government securities, in exchange for privileged access to RBI's primary auctions and related facilities.

children.text: It is tempting to assume banks play the same central market making role in India that they do in some other markets, but in Indian equity and index derivatives specifically, that role is dominated by the proprietary trading firms above, not bank trading desks. Banks are far more central in two other markets. The RBI's

system gives designated banks and institutions an explicit regulatory mandate to underwrite and continuously quote government securities, making them the closest Indian equivalent to a formally mandated bank market making desk, just in bonds rather than equity derivatives. Large banks are also naturally significant liquidity providers in USDINR and other currency pairs, since currency trading is core to their ordinary business of serving corporate and institutional clients' foreign exchange needs, distinct from the standalone, quant-driven market making business model covered throughout this course.
LES-Appointed Market Makers: A Specific, Contracted Role

Chapter 1 covered SEBI's Liquidity Enhancement Scheme, under which exchanges appoint specific entities as market makers for identified illiquid contracts. This is not a separate category of firm so much as a contracted role: a proprietary trading firm or a broker-affiliated desk that already has the infrastructure to quote continuously can take on this specific obligation, in exchange for the exchange's fee waivers and incentives, layering a defined regulatory relationship on top of its ordinary market making business.

body.caption: Who runs market making books in India, by category

cells: Equity index options and futures; also currency and commodity derivatives
Own capital, quant and speed-driven, competes directly on pricing and infrastructure
Explicit regulatory obligation to underwrite and quote two-way markets in bonds
Market making as a byproduct of core corporate forex service, not a standalone business
Specific illiquid stock options and futures
A contracted obligation layered onto an existing prop or broker desk's business

body.text: The single most important distinction for anyone planning a career in this space is that these categories are not interchangeable stepping stones to the same job. A quant researcher role at an equity-derivatives HFT firm and a market making desk at a bank's treasury are genuinely different careers, with different skill emphases, different regulatory environments, and different day-to-day work, even though both are described loosely as market making.

body.title: Two Different Students, Two Different Targets
body.scenario: One student is specifically interested in building and running quantitative pricing models for Nifty and Bank Nifty options. Another is specifically interested in government bond markets and fixed income.
body.prompt: Which category of employer from this lesson should each student primarily target, and why would it be a mistake for either of them to treat all four categories as interchangeable?
body.modelAnswer: The first student should primarily target proprietary trading and HFT firms, since equity index options and futures market making in India is dominated by that category, and the quantitative pricing and speed-focused skills this course has covered are exactly what those firms compete on. The second student should primarily target RBI Primary Dealers, since that is the category with an explicit, regulated mandate to make markets specifically in government securities. Treating all four categories as interchangeable would be a mistake because each has a genuinely different instrument focus, regulatory basis, and business model; a bond-focused Primary Dealer role and a Nifty options prop trading role require overlapping but distinct skills, and neither desk is likely to be hiring for the other's core function.

body.title: The Closest Indian Equivalent to a Bank Market Making Desk
body.question: According to this lesson, what is the closest Indian equivalent to a formally mandated bank market making desk, and in what market?
options: A bank's equity derivatives desk, mandated by SEBI to quote Nifty options
An RBI Primary Dealer, mandated to underwrite and make two-way markets in government securities
A retail broker's client-facing trading desk
An LES-appointed market maker on a stock option
body.explanation: The RBI Primary Dealer system is the clearest example of a bank or bank-like institution carrying an explicit, regulator-granted obligation to make continuous two-way markets, but that obligation applies to government securities, not equity derivatives, where proprietary trading firms are the dominant players instead.

points: Equity and index derivatives market making in India is dominated by proprietary trading and HFT firms trading their own capital, not by bank desks
RBI's Primary Dealer system is the clearest example of an explicit, regulator-mandated bank-like market making obligation in India, but it applies to government securities, not equities

Banks are naturally significant liquidity providers in currency markets like USDINR, as a byproduct of their core corporate foreign exchange business rather than as a standalone market making operation
LES-appointed market makers are not a separate type of firm; they are a contracted regulatory role that a prop firm or broker desk takes on for specific illiquid contracts
These four categories have genuinely different instrument focuses, regulatory bases, and business models, and are not interchangeable career targets
